reason: E1 supports the first two premises by demonstrating that tailored thermo-mechanical processing creates an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with improved strength-ductility synergy. However, E1 does not address creep resistance, and E2 only shows that the unprocessed alloy's passive film is unstable at high temperatures, providing no evidence that the proposed processing improves corrosion behavior. The combined conditions of extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term loading, and corrosion are not covered by the cited evidence.
premises: Thermo-mechanical processing can refine the lamellar structure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 into an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure
This refined duplex microstructure enhances strength and ductility via a two-hierarchical constraint effect and microcrack-arresting mechanism
The refined microstructure will improve room-temperature creep resistance
The refined microstructure will improve corrosion resistance and passive film stability under temperature fluctuations
